payload.body:
The workflow 'tests' failed on GitHub Actions and nothing else would have told you.

  repo:     dk-forge/talent-intelligence-tracker
  workflow: tests
  branch:   fix/companion-region-deadline
  trigger:  pull_request
  run:      https://github.com/dk-forge/talent-intelligence-tracker/actions/runs/31462117064

WHAT FAILED:
  assert (0 == 1)

Context from the failed step:
  FAILED tests/test_ci_noise_report.py::TestMain::test_a_noisy_week_posts_exactly_one_alert - AssertionError: one summary, never one post per run
  FAILED tests/test_ci_noise_report.py::TestMain::test_dry_run_posts_nothing_even_when_noisy - AssertionError: assert (0 == 0 and not [] and '--- subject ---' in 'window: 0 completed runs / 7 days\nfailed: 0  repeats: 0  evictions: 0  noise: 0\nquiet week: no repeat reds, no evictions — nothing to send, and that silence is the product working.\n')
  FAILED tests/test_ci_noise_report.py::TestMain::test_noise_with_no_credentials_is_loud_not_silent - assert (0 == 1)
  +  where 0 = len([])
  AssertionError: assert (0 == 0 and not [] and '--- subject ---' in 'window: 0 completed runs / 7 days\nfailed: 0  repeats: 0  evictions: 0  noise: 0\nquiet week: no repeat reds, no evictions — nothing to send, and that silence is the product working.\n')

What to do: open a Claude Code session in the talent-intelligence-tracker repo and paste this line:
  "The GitHub Actions workflow 'tests' is failing on fix/companion-region-deadline with: assert (0 == 1). The run is https://github.com/dk-forge/talent-intelligence-tracker/actions/runs/31462117064. Reproduce it locally with `.venv/bin/pytest -q`, find the root cause, and fix it."

You will get ONE more email about this workflow: a RECOVERED notice on its next green run. We suppress repeats of this same failure deliberately. An alarm that mails eight times in an afternoon is one you learn to filter, and a filtered alarm is how a wrong number stays live for hours.

entries.repaired_because: key ci-noise:2026-W32 was rejected 400 'bad dedupe_key' 16 times: /alert accepts ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:._-]{0,159}$ and the ISO week carried an uppercase W. Rewritten to ci-noise:2026-w32; ci_noise_report.py now composes %G-w%V. Attempts zeroed because this is a different, deliverable key, and leaving it past FAIL_LOUD_ATTEMPTS would keep host-watch red on an alert that is about to succeed.
